title: An unmapped Shop supplies item shows the warning on the Shop supplies row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Make sure the General Internal category has a QuickBooks expense account at the test location (note its name).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the Shop supplies item in QuickBooks Products And Services has no income account mapped.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Shop supplies row carries the warning that the entry posts to the ShopView Review account until an account is set.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S3-N4: “If no account is mapped for the work order's classification (for a no-charge work order in QuickBooks, no account for the work order's category), the confirmation of S3-R2 replaces the account note with: QuickBooks, "No account set for [category]. The entry posts to the ShopView Review account until you set one." with a "Set account" link to Integrations > QuickBooks; AccountingHub, "No account set for [category]. The entry is held in Accounting Events until you set one." with a link to Account Mappings. The link is shown only to users with 'Settings — Integrations' (QuickBooks) or 'Accounting — Settings' (AccountingHub); others see the note without the link. The Shop supplies row follows the same rule when the Shop supplies item is not mapped (S10-N2). The button still reads "Close Work Order" and closes as in S3-R3. At a QuickBooks location without Inventory Asset or Cost of Parts, the parts rows carry the note of S7-N5 instead.”
  • S10-N2: “If the Shop supplies item is not mapped in QuickBooks, the credit posts to the ShopView Review account as any unmapped account does; if its income account was deleted or made inactive, the entry fails into QB Unexported as every other row's does (S7-N2); in AccountingHub an empty Shop supplies expense row holds the event (S8-N2).”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Close with no account mapped, AccountingHub or shop supplies variants | "No account set for [category]. The entry is held in Accounting Events until you set one." / the Shop supplies row note with the same text | Same warning box”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Internal Work Orders · All flows v6" (https://claude.ai/artifact/5jHR3nLeDinzks1viREFuo), version 1794484794-2031, read and rendered 12 Nov 2026: boards "7b Close · no account set" (page "Flow 1 · Create and close"), "7f Close · QuickBooks without inventory accounts" (page "Flow 1 · Create and close"). Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

  • iwo-flow1-21-7f-close-quickbooks-without-inventory-accounts.png

  • “Parts cost is not posted to QuickBooks at this location: inventory accounts are not mapped.”

Difference IWO-D22 on S3-N4 (wording): settled by the PRD (S3-N4); this case follows the PRD.
